People in India are switching to UPI because paying now takes a few seconds and works almost everywhere, from big shops to the chai stall at the corner. You link your bank account once, and after that a scan and a PIN is all it takes. There are no cards to carry and no cash to count out.

It is instant and usually free. Money moves from your bank to theirs right away, at any hour, including Sundays and holidays. Everyday payments between people and to most shops carry no charge.
It works across apps and banks. Whether you use PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm or your bank's own app, you can pay anyone. A shop needs just one QR code to accept all of them.
It suits small payments. Paying ₹20 is as easy as paying ₹5,000 so street vendors, auto drivers and tiny shops accept it, and nobody hunts for change.

Add a PIN for every payment and the fact that friends and family already use it, and cash starts to feel like the slower option. Once a few people around you switch, the rest tend to follow quickly.
